solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rejected sweets, under pressure

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the word for sweets is read backwards

parts.note: desserts are sweet courses

explanation.surface: Someone pushes away the pudding course because they are feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns DESSERTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a person feeling strain and tension is said to be stressed.

clue.text: Sympathetic to number one spy, I felt moved

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for a noun: sorrow felt for oneself

indicators.note: moved letters are shifted into new places, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy confesses to being touched by compassion for his chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like emotion but rearranges SPY I FELT. 'number one' is oneself, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallowing in sorrow over one's own troubles is feeling sorry for oneself.

clue.text: Go to the top of steps in preparation for delivery

definitions.text: Go to the top of steps

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the bowler's approach before releasing the ball

explanation.surface: Climbing the stairs as part of getting ready to hand over a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's 'delivery' is a ball bowled, preceded by an approach run.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for dashing upstairs, and the cricket noun for a bowler's approach.

clue.text: Colleague making nurse go crazy

indicators.note: crazy suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hospital workmate who drives the nursing staff mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges NURSE GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre doctor is a hospital co-worker of a nurse, the definition leaning on the surface.

clue.text: Swine leaves birds for ages

indicators.note: the swine word departs from the bird word

parts.note: pigeons are birds
a pig is a swine

explanation.surface: A pig abandons a flock of birds for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes PIG out of PIGEONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast stretches of time; informally, a very long while.

clue.text: Meagre spread — odd bits of corn garnished with mushy peas

indicators.note: the corn letters are dressed all round with the pea letters, so one piece encloses the other
mushy peas are mashed up, so these letters are rearranged
the odd-numbered letters of corn, the first and third, are taken

explanation.surface: A poor meal: a few kernels of corn served with mushy peas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' signals the anagram, 'odd bits of' the letter selection, and 'garnished with' the wrapping of one around the other. 'spread' is butter thinly scraped on.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is a thin smearing of butter or the like on bread, a meagre spread.

clue.text: Upset, head will have a fit if this is right!

definitions.text: head will have a fit if this is right!
definitions.meaning: if the measurement of a hat is correct, it fits the head

explanation.surface: An angry boss will throw a tantrum if this is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have a fit' looks like a tantrum but means a hat fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a vessel, and the measurement of a hat, read as two words.

clue.text: Part of mean tip, a stingy Italian diner might offer these

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A miserly customer leaves a meagre gratuity at an Italian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' gives the run of letters inside 'mean tip, a stingy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian starters such as cured meats and olives, served before the main course.

clue.text: Unruly teen with aggression outwardly of one blowing top?

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are jumbled
only the outside letters, first and last, of aggression are used

explanation.surface: A disorderly adolescent showing temper, the sort who blows his top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges TEEN to ETNE; 'outwardly' takes AN from aggression. The one blowing its top is a volcano, Etna.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Etna, the Sicilian volcano that erupts, or blows its top.

clue.text: Extended passion bridge partner's held from a distance

parts.note: extended means long

indicators.note: the bridge player is held within the word for passion

parts.note: a passion can be a fit of rage
N, North, is one of the four bridge players, partnered with South

explanation.surface: A bridge player's partner keeps up a long outburst at them from across the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts N inside RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range describes weapons or shots that act over a great distance.

clue.text: Heading in goal with power?

indicators.note: the heading goes inside the goal word

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
a title is a heading

explanation.surface: A footballer scoring with a powerful header.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture is false: 'goal' is an aim and 'Heading' a caption; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a right or authority to something; the question mark flags the loose synonym.

clue.text: Install powerful leader

definitions.meaning: to install something is to put it in place

explanation.surface: Fit in a strongman as head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym for fitting, and the surname of Russia's dominant president.

clue.text: Two peas reportedly — note where you'd see them burst out

indicators.note: the pod sits on the outside, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: peas are found in a pod

indicators.note: the letters are said to sound like the words two peas, a pair of P sounds

parts.note: two letter P's, which sound like peas
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A pair of peas in their shell, waiting to pop out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes 'Two peas' the sound of two letter P's; 'out' places the pod around them and the note.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something that has popped has burst open with a small bang.

clue.text: African state gets this cop's bias exposed, serially

indicators.note: each word in turn is stripped of its outer letters, exposing its inside

explanation.surface: A country is accused of police prejudice being uncovered, case after case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed, serially' takes the insides of each word in turn: ET, HI, OP, IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Old correspondent exchanging last letters — attention finally undivided

indicators.note: the final two letters of the correspondent swap places

parts.note: a pen pal writes letters

indicators.note: only the last letter of attention is taken

explanation.surface: An elderly letter-writer swaps the final letters, giving full attention at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging last letters' turns PENPAL into PENPLA; 'finally' gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: An office laid out without partition walls is one undivided space.

clue.text: Teaches throwing perhaps to geeks

parts.note: to train is to teach
potters throw pots on a wheel, so those throwing could be potters

explanation.surface: Coaching someone in a throwing sport is supposedly attractive to nerds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throwing' looks like sport, but it is shaping clay on a potter's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway enthusiasts who log engine numbers are the stock British image of obsessive nerds.

clue.text: One broadcasting from a twelfth-century church interior

indicators.note: the church abbreviation sits inside the Norman word

parts.note: Norman architecture and rule marks England around the twelfth century

explanation.surface: A presenter reports from inside an old Romanesque church.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman (Romanesque) building style dominated English churches of the twelfth century; 'interior' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A news presenter who fronts a broadcast and links reports.

clue.text: Mum holds up one article after another repeatedly as something loathsome

indicators.note: in a down answer the mum word sits below, holding the articles up

parts.note: the articles an, a and the strung together
ma is mum

explanation.surface: A mother keeps holding up one item after another as dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' puts MA beneath ANATHE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing detested or abhorred, originally a thing cursed by the church.

clue.text: Sequence inevitably following flush?

parts.note: a self-sustaining series of events; pulling an old toilet's chain to flush brings a response from the plumbing

explanation.surface: What follows when someone pulls the lavatory handle.
explanation.walkthrough: Old toilets are flushed by pulling a chain, so the cascade that follows is what the chain sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence of events each causing the next is a domino effect, here split as the response to a pulled chain.

clue.text: Governed during uprising, in painful chaos

indicators.note: the governing word comes within the painful one

parts.note: achy means painful

indicators.note: in a down answer an uprising reads bottom to top

parts.note: to run a country is to govern it

explanation.surface: A regime ruled throughout a revolt amid agonising disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses the governing word upwards in this down entry; 'during' sets it inside the painful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawlessness and disorder, the absence of government.

clue.text: What Richard III wanted, perhaps that would prevent loss of power?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's king cries 'My kingdom for a horse!', wanting a warhorse

definitions.text: perhaps that would prevent loss of power?
definitions.meaning: a device topping up a battery stops it going flat

explanation.surface: The king's need at Bosworth might have kept him in power.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry warhorse, and a device for recharging batteries.

clue.text: Port, old, handed round unopened

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters are read backwards
the first letter is removed

parts.note: passed means handed over

explanation.surface: An old bottle of port passed round the table without being uncorked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine but is a harbour. 'unopened' drops the first letter (leaving ASSED) and 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea seaport in Ukraine.

clue.text: Hang around outside toilet, turning crazy

indicators.note: the loitering word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to dally is to loiter or hang about

indicators.note: turning means the toilet word is read back to front

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Someone loitering by a public lavatory goes a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses the toilet word and 'outside' wraps the loitering word round it. LOO is everyday British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for mad or unhinged, from an Indian army camp name.

clue.text: Tap dancing cue — enter during 'Grease'

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside the word for grease

parts.note: grease is fat

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so cue is rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage cue for a tap number in the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tap' and 'dancing' sit together as tap dancing but are split: 'dancing' is the anagram signal, and 'enter during' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for a water tap or spigot.

clue.text: Labour and Conservative leaders turning up in secret council

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: LAB is the short form of the UK Labour Party

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Heads of the two main British parties appear at a clandestine meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' gives A and C; 'turning up' reverses LABAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a small group of plotters meeting in secret.

clue.text: Man United forwards resurgent after 0-5, showing a bit of life potentially

indicators.note: the reversed piece follows the scoreline letters

parts.note: 0 looks like the letter O and 5 is V in Roman numerals

indicators.note: rising again, in a down answer read upwards
the leading letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Manchester United's strikers fight back after being five down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forwards' gives MU from Man United, and 'resurgent' turns it to UM.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cell, which if fertilised could become a new living being.

clue.text: Spice French novelist brought from East

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: Albert Camus, author of The Outsider

explanation.surface: A French author fetches spices back from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought from East' reads CAMUS from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a tangy red berry ground into a seasoning used in Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Presumably deep enough for the Spanish carrier, and Russian, heading to port

indicators.note: port is the left side, so the pieces are read right to left

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a bag carries things
Ivan is a typical Russian man's name

explanation.surface: Is the water deep enough for a Spanish aircraft carrier and a Russian ship to sail to harbour?
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to port' (going left) reverses ELBAGIVAN. 'for the Spanish carrier' looks like part of the definition, but supplies wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that ships can pass through must be of sufficient depth, hence the 'presumably'.

clue.text: Something loud audibly grates

indicators.note: says the letters are what is heard when the phrase is spoken

parts.note: a noise is something loud

explanation.surface: A loud din is heard to set one's teeth on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' turns 'a noise' into a word of the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something that grates irritates or vexes people.

clue.text: Deviously lure lamb into shelter

indicators.note: devious means roundabout, so the letters take a winding new order

explanation.surface: Someone cunningly tempts a lamb into a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deviously' rearranges LURE and LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly gives cover from rain, and the word also means protective cover more widely.
